# NIST AI Risk Management Framework — Overview

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management
Framework (AI RMF 1.0) is a voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific
framework to improve the ability to incorporate trustworthiness
considerations into the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI
products, services, and systems.

## Four core functions

The AI RMF is organized around four functions:

- **Govern** — cultivate a culture of risk management; establish policies,
  processes, procedures, and practices.
- **Map** — establish the context and classify the AI system.
- **Measure** — analyze, assess, benchmark, and monitor AI risks and their
  impacts.
- **Manage** — allocate risk resources to mapped and measured risks on a
  regular basis and as defined by the Govern function.

## Characteristics of trustworthy AI

Trustworthy AI systems are: valid and reliable; safe; secure and resilient;
accountable and transparent; explainable and interpretable; privacy-enhanced;
and fair with harmful bias managed.

## Scope and applicability

The framework is voluntary and applies across all sectors. It is designed to
be used by organizations of any size, in any sector, and throughout any
portion of the AI lifecycle.
